chunks: With this chain of narration, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, gives the world to whom He loves and to whom He dislikes, but He gives the Hereafter only to whom He loves. Indeed, the believer asks his Lord for a place of a lash in the world, yet He does not give it to him, and he asks Him for the Hereafter, so He gives him whatever he wishes. And He gives the disbeliever from the world before he asks Him for whatever He wishes, and he asks Him for a place of a lash in the Hereafter, so He does not give it to him.

key_terms.إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He
key_terms.مَوْضِعَ سَوْطٍ: A place of a lash, a small spot

ai.summary: This hadith highlights the divine wisdom in distributing worldly versus eternal rewards. While Allah grants the transient world to both the beloved and the disliked, the Hereafter is exclusive to those He loves. The believer is characterized by patience, often forgoing even a small portion of worldly pleasure to secure abundant rewards in the Hereafter, whereas the disbeliever is granted worldly pleasures abundantly in advance but is denied even a minimal share of the Hereafter.

en.badr-shahin: (The same previous series of relaters)… that Abu Ja’far (a) said:

Allah, Powerful and Majestic is He, gives (the pleasures of) this world to anyone, whether He likes or dislikes, while He gives the world to come only to those whom He likes. It happens that Allah does not answer the believer who asks for a location that is as small as a place of a lash, and gives the world to the disbeliever before he asks for anything. But, if that disbeliever asks Allah for a location that is as small as a place of a lash in the world to come, Allah will not answer him.
